newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwean shares continue firmer on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwean shares continue firmer on Wednesday.

text.p: Zimbabwe's industrial shares traded firmer on Wednesday on the back of improved liquidity and market speculation on a lower than expected May inflation figure, brokers said.
"The market is showing increased liquidity coupled with a reluctance to sell at these (current) low levels, and as a result, second tier shares are firming," one broker commented.
"The market rumour of a lower than expected inflation figure for May could also account for some of the firming," the broker added.

The key industrial index climbed 64.37 points higher to 10,294.28, riding on stronger deals in agricultural investors Chemco which surged 450 cents to 4,500, with bankers FMB 200 cents firmer at 4,100 and pharmaceutical group Caps up 100 cents at 2,700.

Hoteliers and retailers Meikles and clothing chain Edgars both added 50 cents to 2,700 and 750 respectively, and clothing and furniture retailers Tedco put on 30 cents to 270. Haulage firm Clan and horticultural group Ariston, both quoted at 190, were up 10 cents.
Minings were generally lifeless with Falgold trading unchanged while coal miners Wankie crept up five cents to 570. The secondary mining index inched 1.82 points up to 999.70.
